data.gender_notes: Vasu is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Vasu is a class of deities associated with the earth and protectors of the universe. Vasus are the guardians of the elements and preside over various natural phenomena. They are also revered as the protectors of houses and homes. The name Vasu carries the meaning “Dwelling, Abode, Residence” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vasu usually hope their child will grow to embody dwelling, abode, residence and live with faith, good character and purpose.

vedic_reference.note: Vasus are 84 divine beings in Hindu mythology, also called Vasus or Vasu-sahasranama. They are considered the guardians of various natural elements like earth, water, air, and fire. In the Rigveda, the hymn to Vasus mentions them as the 'shining ones' or 'luminous ones'.

historical_references.reference: The Vasus are a group of Hindu deities regarded as the guardians of the directions and the dwellers of the various cosmic spaces. They are mentioned in the Rigveda, the earliest existing Hindu scripture, where they are described as the 'Gods of the earth'.

Vasu is also the name of a minor god in Hinduism who is believed to reside in the human heart. According to Hindu mythology, Vasu, along with other gods, resides in the heart and protects the body from all harms. This belief is reflected in the Upanishads, the Hindu scriptures composed between 800 BCE and 500 BCE.

It can be seen on Instagram, where users may use the name as a handle or hashtag in relation to spiritual or mythological content. On Twitter, users may use the name in a similar context, or as a tribute to Hindu deities or mythological figures. On LinkedIn, professionals with the name 'Vasu' may use it as part of their online identity and professional branding. The name 'Vasu' is also associated with the trend of spiritual names, which are becoming increasingly popular in modern society as people seek to connect with their spiritual side and express their cultural heritage.
